paragraphs: An ML-powered operations service that detects anomalous application behaviour and recommends fixes, with reactive and proactive insights; it stops accepting new customers on October 29, 2026 and ends support on September 30, 2027.
2 min read · Last reviewed 3 November 2026 · MLA-C02

Amazon DevOps Guru is a fully managed operations service that uses machine learningML (Machine learning)Software that learns patterns from example data to make predictions or decisions, instead of following rules written by hand. A model is first trained on data, then used to make predictions on new data, which is called inference.Glossary entryClose to analyze operational data, application metrics, and events, find behaviour that deviates from normal patterns, and recommend fixes. It creates reactive insights for problems happening now (for example rising latencyLatencyThe time between sending a request and receiving the response, usually measured in milliseconds. Distance and processing add to it; caching and serving users from nearby locations reduce it.Glossary entryClose and errors after a deployment) and proactive insights for risks that could cause problems later.

Availability: DevOps Guru stops accepting new customers on October 29, 2026. Existing customers can keep using it until September 30, 2027, after which it can no longer be accessed. The MLA-C02 exam lists it in scope, so recognize it; for new designs, use the alternatives below.
IAM controls access; DevOps Guru reads CloudWatch, CloudTrail, and Config data in your account; insights are encrypted.
Its value is faster detection of operational issues, which shortens outages.
ML baselines adapt to each metric, which reduces the threshold tuning that static alarms need.

Charged by the resource hours analyzed and the APIAPI (Application programming interface)A defined way for one program to ask another for data or actions, such as a set of HTTPS requests and responses. Every AWS service is controlled through its API, which the console, the CLI, and the SDKs call for you.Glossary entryClose calls made; set coverage to None in each account and RegionAWS RegionA separate geographic area where AWS runs its services, such as us-east-1 in Northern Virginia, made up of several Availability Zones. Most resources live in one Region; you choose Regions for latency, data residency, and the services you need.Glossary entryClose to stop charges.
Insights appear in the console and are sent through SNS and EventBridge.
